author: blu
body: The NE2000 is the default and stays the default. Nothing binds the Intel part unless net-driver-bind-e1000 is called at bring-up, so a guest that never probes PCI behaves exactly as it did before this chapter learned a second card.

author: blu
body: The card selector is written LAST. Until it is, a half-written control block is never the live one, so a bind that faults partway through leaves the NE2000 serving rather than a card with three of its six addresses set.

author: blu
body: A card whose station address is absent is REFUSED, and that is the reason the bind takes a device rather than six integers. RAH bit 31 is the address-valid bit and E1000e reports a clear one rather than inventing an address; a card the network cannot answer is worse than no card, because the frames leave and the replies are filtered out by the card itself, which reads as a dead link.

author: blu
body: It scans the whole bus TREE, not bus 0. This asked `pci-scan-bus 0` when it was written, which finds a chipset-integrated part and silently misses a discrete one behind a bridge, and a silent miss here lands on a NE2000 that does not exist outside the emulator. Measured under OVMF, the NIC is at `01:00.0` with only the bridge on bus 0, so the firmware we gate against is a case that bus 0 alone gets wrong.

author: blu
body: Every refusal lands on the NE2000. A bus with no matching part answers None; a part that fails reset comes back from `e1000-init` as `e1000-absent`; a part whose station address is invalid is refused by `net-driver-bind-e1000`. In all three the selector is never written, so a program that calls this on a machine it does not recognise behaves exactly as it did before the call existed.

author: blu
body: The address every outgoing frame is sourced from, and the one the card's own receive filter is programmed with. They have to be the same value or the card discards the replies before the driver is called.

author: blu
body: The NE2000 answer is a declared constant because there is nothing to read: the part exists only inside codex-vm, and this is the address its NAT is built to expect. That is why the value was never wrong while the NE2000 was the only card.
